newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Hotel Melia privatization delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Hotel Melia privatization delayed again.

text.p: The auction of Venezuela's five-star, unfinished and state-owned Hotel Melia has been postponed for the third time this year, until early next month, officials said.
"We're practically organizing a new sale and we hope to conclude it on December 6," Roberto Piol told Reuters. Piol is president of Banco Industrial de Venezuela (BIV), which owns the building.
The base price for what is potentially one of the largest and most luxurious hotel complexes in Latin America has been fixed at about $33 million.
Piol said it was a new auction because the BIV was again inviting all 51 local and foreign companies that have shown interest in the hotel to take part in the bidding.
Construction of the 624-room Melia in central Caracas began in 1987, but was stopped in 1994 when the then-owner could not meet bank payments and the property was transferred to the BIV.
